title: a self task's own design/tasks file in the worktree always carries the pinned spec bytes, so a captain-approved repin reaches the branch without firstmate briefing it
acceptance: Why. Gate 4 (`fm_pin scope`, bin/lib/fm_spec_pins.py:516-534) checks a self task's branch against the latest pin: the branch's own `design/tasks/<id>.json` must equal the pinned spec text byte for byte (`self task entry differs from pin`, :521-526), and every changed path must match the pinned scope (:527-532). That is the right authority: a pin only changes through `bin/fm-project.sh repin` with an exact captain decision (§15.5). But nothing brings a repinned spec into the branch. fm-worker.sh copies the task file into the worktree only for an unpinned first round (bin/fm-worker.sh:606-639: the `[ -z "$FM_SPEC_PIN_JSON" ]` guard at :622), and a rebuilt round restores the previous head's bytes (`rebuild_entry` at :1066, `rebuild_own_file_restore` :968-976, the pre-commit `rebuild_lost index` check :1888-1895). So on 2026-10-05 T-196: the captain widened the scope on card D-firstmate-workflow-T196-2, firstmate repinned (state/pins/T-196/2.json), round 2 fixed the code inside the new scope, and gate 4 stayed red because the PR still carried the old `design/tasks/T-196.json`; a whole round 3 existed only to commit the pinned file, briefed by hand. A rebuilt round makes it worse: it actively restores the old bytes. This task makes the launcher put the pinned bytes in place itself.

Decision: the worker launcher syncs the file; gate 4 does not change. Gate 4 keeps comparing the branch file and the diff with the pin, so it never accepts a scope nobody approved; the pin stays the only authority, and the branch file becomes its committed copy. Making gate 4 ignore the branch file instead was rejected: the PR and main would then carry a task file whose scope differs from what was approved and merged.

Sync at round start, for the worker's view. In bin/fm-worker.sh, for a self project (`FM_EXTERNAL=0`) with a verified pin, define `pinned_path` = `.snapshots.spec.path` and `pinned_bytes` = the exact `.snapshots.spec.text`, held in a scratch file written with `jq -j .snapshots.spec.text > <scratch>` (never `jq -r`, which appends a newline, and never a `$(...)` capture, which strips the file's trailing newline); every comparison is `cmp -s <scratch> <file>`; if `pinned_path` is not `design/tasks/<TASK>.json`, exit 65 naming both. Every read of the pinned text uses exactly the argv `jq -j .snapshots.spec.text` (tests inject failures on that argv). The sync point is immediately after the pin block (:1101-1124), so a first pin created this round (:1107) is included; it is skipped in a rebuilt round (`rebuilt=1`), where the rebuild restore below is the one writer. If the round's HEAD has no `$pinned_path` (a new task whose earlier rounds published nothing), the file is treated exactly as the T-147 copy: written from the scratch file, `spec_copied=1` with its scratch copy, excluded from the round's work, the T-147 prompt paragraph, and `pin_synced` stays 0. Otherwise, if `$tree/$pinned_path` is not byte-identical to `pinned_bytes`, write it (creating `design/tasks/`), set `pin_synced=1` (the branch carried an older approved spec), keep the pin version for messages, and print to stderr `fm-worker: design/tasks/<TASK>.json follows pin v<N>; written into the worktree for this round to commit`. No event type is added. The mirror baseline (`mirror_sync`, :1099) is taken before this point; a later `mirror_restore` can therefore bring back the pre-sync file, which the post-adapter step below repairs, so the start sync is never the only guarantee. An unpinned round and an external round are unchanged, including the T-147 copy at :606-639; when that copy already holds the pinned bytes the sync is a no-op.

The sync counts as work only when it actually changed the file. While the vendor chain runs, `worker_changed_files` (:1298-1313) excludes the synced file exactly as it excludes the T-147 copy (a scratch copy of `pinned_bytes` and the `cmp` at :1305-1309), so `fm_run_chain`'s `worker_did_work` predicate (:1409) never mistakes the sync for a vendor's work: an unavailable vendor (exit 2) with that predicate true is taken as used, not skipped (bin/fm-config.sh:800-801), which would end fallback. Post-adapter step, for a pinned self round that was not rebuilt, placed right after the 'every vendor was unavailable' exit 2 at :1457 (that is, after `. "$chain_result"`, its unknown-vendor and model-refusal exits at :1425-1446, the transport exit 70 at :1447, the misread/skipped handling at :1448-1456 and `report_blocked_hosts`), and before any publish decision (:1712-1811): if `$tree/design/tasks/<TASK>.json` is not byte-identical to `pinned_bytes` (the worker edited it, or a mirror restore brought back the old file), write `pinned_bytes` again and, when the worker had changed it, print `fm-worker: design/tasks/<TASK>.json restored to pin v<N>; a task file changes only by repin`. Then set `pin_counts=1` only if `pin_synced=1` (the start sync found the worktree file different from the pin, i.e. the branch carried an older approved spec); only then does `worker_changed_files` stop excluding it, so a round where the worker changed nothing else still commits and pushes the task file with the round's normal commit message (:1950) through the existing publish path, and the T-196 round-3 case needs no brief. A restore alone never sets `pin_counts`: in a first round whose file came from the T-147 copy (not on HEAD) the T-147 exclusion stays in force, so §5.2a's rule 'a round that leaves it as it was and changes nothing else changed nothing' holds. No non-rebuilt round exits 75 because of the task file. Early exits never publish the sync alone: on every exit taken before the post-adapter step (the 65 exits at :1425-1446, the transport exit 70 at :1447, exit 2 when every vendor was unavailable at :1457, a signal, or any earlier error), `publish_wip_if_dirty` (:224-265, called from the `finished` trap) first puts the task file back as HEAD has it (`git -C "$tree" checkout -- design/tasks/<TASK>.json`, or removes it when HEAD has none) whenever `pin_synced=1` or the file came from the start sync, before it computes `dirty`; so a round where no vendor ran pushes nothing, consistent with the guarantee at :462-465 that an unavailable vendor touches nothing. Once the post-adapter step has run, the trap leaves the file as the round has it.

Rebuilt rounds freeze to the pin, not to the previous head. A rebuild only happens in a later round (`round_two=1`), which already has a pin loaded at :366, except a legacy unpinned branch whose first pin is created on resume at :1107 from the approved branch spec: those bytes equal the branch's file, so the previous-head rule and the pin rule agree and the rebuild keeps today's behaviour for it. When the pin is loaded before `bring_up_to_date` (:1094) and the round is self: the frozen entry is the pin's exact bytes, compared byte for byte (not the `jq -cS` form, which would leave a reformatted file that gate 4 refuses): `rebuild_own_file_restore` (:968-976) writes `pinned_bytes` (via the single `jq -j .snapshots.spec.text` read) instead of `git show <old head>:<file>` whenever the worktree file is not byte-identical to them, and stages it, before `rebuild_mark` is taken (:1089), so the file is part of the rebuild and published through `rebuild_publishes` (:1328-1330); `rebuild_lost` (:958-966) compares worktree and index bytes with `pinned_bytes`. A failed write leaves the entry lost, which is unresolved like a marker, as today. The worker test fixtures (`fixture()`, tests/lib/worker.sh:46-72, and `rb_build_fixture`, tests/lib/worker-rebuild.sh:47-58) write no captain approval, so their rounds are unpinned (fm_spec_pins.py:115-144 returns no approval; fm-worker.sh:1112 'no pin') and every existing unpinned rebuild case keeps today's rule and text unchanged. A worker that changes the file in a rebuilt round is still refused by the existing pre-commit check (:1888-1895, exit 75, nothing published, `rebuild_refuse`), now with text naming the pin when pinned: `the task's own entry is not as pin v<N> has it in: <file>` / `任務自己的條目跟 pin v<N> 不一樣：<file>`. The post-adapter repair above does not run in rebuilt rounds, so this refusal stays the one path there. Unpinned rebuilds keep today's previous-head rule and text.

The prompt. When `pin_synced=1`, one paragraph in the task section (next to the T-147 paragraph at :1198-1203) says firstmate's approved spec changed (pin v<N>), the launcher wrote it into the worktree, it is committed with the round, and the worker must leave it as it is. Every pinned self round's prompt says the task file follows the pin and is restored to the pin if edited (in a rebuilt round: an edit holds the round). In a pinned self rebuilt round, the two rebuild prompt sentences that name the previous head change to name the pin: `Put it back exactly as it is at $rebuild_prev, keeping $BASE's other changes.` (:1266) becomes `Put it back exactly as pin v<N> has it (the approved spec at <FM_PINNED_DIR>/spec.json), keeping $BASE's other changes.`, and `Your task file design/tasks/<TASK>.json must come through exactly as it is at $rebuild_prev; a rebuilt round that changes it is refused, like one that leaves a conflict marker.` (:1268-1270) becomes `... must come through exactly as pin v<N> has it; a rebuilt round that changes it is refused, like one that leaves a conflict marker.` Unpinned rebuilt rounds keep both sentences byte for byte (tests/worker-rebuild-publication.test.sh:205, V6, unchanged).

Tests, in a new suite tests/spec-pin-sync.test.sh built on tests/lib/worker.sh (and tests/lib/worker-rebuild.sh for the rebuild cases). Its rounds are pinned the way tests/spec-pin-worker.test.sh:6-10 and tests/spec-preflight-worker.test.sh:10-13 do it: before round one the suite commits `project:\n  check: true` appended to the fixture's config.yaml, plus a `.gitignore` containing `state/`, to main and pushes (a pin snapshots the gate contract, and `contract()` refuses a config with no `project:` block, fm_spec_pins.py:44-58, 169-176), then writes a `greenlit` event with actor `captain` to `state/events.jsonl`, so the first round creates pin v1. A repin is authorised exactly as tests/lib/spec_pins_cases.py:50-54 records a decision: `state/decisions/D-sync.json` = `{id:'D-sync', project:'firstmate-workflow', task:'T-Z', chosen:'A', kind:'choice', ts}` plus a `decision_made` event (actor `captain`, task T-Z, `data:{decision:'D-sync', chosen:'A'}`, same ts), with ts newer than v1's approval (fm_spec_pins.py:503-514). Then the repository's design/tasks/T-Z.json (uncommitted, as a real repin reads it, fm_spec_pins.py:178) gets v2's scope = v1's scope plus `design/tasks/T-Z.json` and `lib/**`, `seed_spec_preflight` records v2's bytes, and `$ROOT/bin/fm-project.sh repin --repo <fixture repo> --project firstmate-workflow --task T-Z --decision D-sync` (bin/fm-project.sh:39-67; `fixture()` does not copy fm-project.sh, so the suite calls the engine's copy with `--repo`) writes v2. Cases:
- (a) Repin reaches the branch: after round one (pin v1, published) and the repin, round two's adapter changes nothing. The pushed head's `design/tasks/T-Z.json` is byte-identical to v2's `.snapshots.spec.text`, the round exits 0, stderr names `follows pin v2`, the prompt names pin v2, and `fm_pin scope --task T-Z --head <head> --base main` (bin/fm-config.sh:1150) succeeds (v2's scope covers the task file, which differs from main's v1). Red on base: the head keeps v1's file and `fm_pin scope` fails with `self task entry differs from pin`.
- (a2) Fallback is not fooled: the suite writes a second adapter `bin/adapters/mock2.sh` into the fixture repo (a test file, no change to any shared stub) and writes its config.yaml as `vendor: mock` / `fallback:` / `  - mock` / `  - mock2` / `project:` / `  check: true` (block list, because `fm_cfg_list`, bin/fm-config.sh:43-48, reads only block items; the `project:` block kept, because the repin and every pin read the local contract), committed and pushed before the repin; round two's `mock` exits 2 without touching the tree; `mock2` is invoked (its marker file exists) and the round publishes v2's bytes. Its 'mock2 is invoked' half holds on base too; its 'publishes v2's bytes' half is red on base.
- (b) An adapter that edits design/tasks/T-Z.json and writes src/feature in a non-rebuilt pinned round: exit 0, the pushed head carries the pinned bytes and src/feature, stderr says `restored to pin v<N>`.
- (b2) Mirror restore: after the v2 repin, an adapter that empties the worktree (the T-MIR pattern of tests/worker-mirror.test.sh :6-42, also used by T-PRESERVE :133 and T-RESTOREPROMPT :163-193) and then writes src/feature; the round exits 0 and publishes, and the pushed head's design/tasks/T-Z.json is byte-identical to v2's text, never v1's, and carries src/feature.
- (e) New task, adapter changes nothing: the suite removes design/tasks/T-Z.json from main after `fixture()` (`git rm --cached`, commit, push), leaving it uncommitted in the repository so dispatch reads it as seeded (fm_spec_pins.py:178); so the task file is not on main; round one (no pin yet at its start, so the T-147 copy runs) creates pin v1, its adapter changes nothing, and today's trap pushes `checkpoint (exit-1)` carrying the copied file (publish_wip_if_dirty, :224-265): assert exactly that (exit 1, one checkpoint commit whose design/tasks/T-Z.json equals pin v1's bytes). Round two then has `spec_only=1` and a pin whose bytes equal HEAD's file: its start sync is a no-op, its adapter changes nothing, it exits 1, no `follows pin` line is printed and no second commit is pushed. A regression guard: base behaves the same.
- (f) Every vendor unavailable after a repin: v2 recorded, round two's only vendor exits 2; the round exits 2, stderr says `every vendor was unavailable`, the remote branch head is unchanged (nothing pushed, not even a checkpoint), and the worktree's task file is back to HEAD's bytes. Red on base only in that base has no sync; it is a regression guard for the trap rule.
- (c) Rebuild after repin. tests/lib/worker-rebuild.sh gains an opt-in `RB_PINNED=1` for `rb_build_fixture` (the default seeds built at source time, :60-61, stay unpinned and unchanged): with it, the builder appends `project:\n  check: true` to config.yaml and adds a `.gitignore` with `state/` in its base commit before pushing main, writes the `greenlit` event before round one, seeds preflight with `seed_spec_preflight <repo> T-Z "" firstmate-workflow`, runs every round (`rb_build_fixture` round one and `rb_round_two`, :106-113) with `--project firstmate-workflow`, and its round-one script omits the `depends_on` edit of design/tasks/T-Z.json (:51), so the seed's head carries pin v1's bytes on base and head alike. The new suite calls `RB_PINNED=1 rb_build_fixture` for its own seed; v2's preflight and the repin use `firstmate-workflow` too. Then main moves so the branch no longer rebases, then the v2 repin; the rebuilt published commit carries v2's bytes, not the previous head's, and no refusal fires.
- (c2) In that pinned rebuilt round, an adapter that edits the task file: exit 75, nothing published, message `not as pin v<N> has it in: design/tasks/T-Z.json`, and its prompt contains `must come through exactly as pin v2 has it` and not the unpinned sentence `must come through exactly as it is at <previous head>` (the rebuild header at :1233, which names the previous head as the branch's prior state, is unchanged).
- (c3) In that pinned rebuilt round, a PATH wrapper for `jq` that exits 1 when its arguments are exactly `-j .snapshots.spec.text`: the restore fails, the entry is reported lost, the round publishes nothing (as V6 does for an unpinned rebuild), and its prompt says `Put it back exactly as pin v2 has it` with the pinned spec path.
- (d) A pinned round whose branch file already equals the pin and whose adapter changes nothing publishes nothing and prints no `follows pin` line (regression guard).
Existing suites are regression guards, unchanged and green on base and head, because their fixtures are unpinned or external, except tests/spec-preflight-worker.test.sh, which is pinned and repins twice (:51-69): its assertions are only about preflight refusals (exit 65 before the adapter, no events, no ref change, :70-74, all before any worktree sync) and that the adapter is called (:77); its last round now also syncs v3 and pushes it, which none of its assertions reads, and its refusal round's remote-ref check runs before any sync. The others: tests/worker-rebuild.test.sh (case I :225-243 and W2 :617-636 keep the previous-head rule and text), tests/worker-rebuild-publication.test.sh (V6 :181-214 keeps its `git show` injection), tests/spec-pin-worker.test.sh, tests/worker-lifecycle.test.sh, tests/worker-notes.test.sh, tests/worker-exits.test.sh, tests/worker-mirror.test.sh, tests/worker-executable.test.sh, tests/lifeline.test.sh, tests/option-loop.test.sh, tests/legacy-pin-repin.test.sh, tests/spec-preflight-worker.test.sh, tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh, tests/external-execution.test.sh and tests/external-review-launchers.test.sh. tests/spec-pin-worker.test.sh's pinned rounds keep a branch file equal to their pin, so the sync is a no-op there. The new suite stays under 1200 lines.

Docs, edited in place (T-189 rule; nothing appended after the last section): design §15.5 'Immutable pins and authoritative heads' (header at design.md:4956) gains two sentences: a self task's branch file is the committed copy of the latest pin, written by fm-worker.sh at round start and committed with the round, a non-rebuilt round restores it to the pin before publishing, and a rebuilt round that changes it is held (exit 75); gate 4 is unchanged. §5.2a's paragraph 'A new task's spec comes with its worktree (T-147)' (:499-511): its sentence 'a rebuilt round's entry stays frozen (5.3.3), so only a new branch gets the copy' says a pinned round's file follows the pin. §5.3.3 (starts :883; the paragraph 'The task's own file ...' at :962-966 and 'nor while the task's own file differs from the previous head's' at :974-977): a pinned round's entry is frozen to the pin, an unpinned one to the previous head.

In flight and migration. No stored record changes shape: pins, evidence and events are untouched, and no event type is added. The only open PR, #159 (T-055), has a branch file byte-identical to its pin v1 (checked 2026-10-05), so its next round is a no-op for this change. Any round started after this merges runs the new launcher (sessions freeze engine code per session, §11); a round already running finishes on the old code. A task whose branch file differs from its pin today gets the pinned bytes committed by its next round, which is exactly the intended repair. The memory-noted case (a scope widening lost in a rebuilt round) is covered by the rebuild rule and test (c).

Workers do not run the suites. Evidence is the required GitHub check and the six gates. Fail-first is expected from tests/spec-pin-sync.test.sh: cases a, a2 (its publish half), b, b2, c, c2 (its message) and c3 (its injection targets a write base does not make) are red on base; d is a regression guard that also holds on base. No shared vendor stub changes: the mock adapter and the gh stub are used as they are; the only shared fixture change is the opt-in `RB_PINNED=1` in tests/lib/worker-rebuild.sh, whose default is unchanged; the suite's second adapter lives only in its own fixture repo. Cases e and f are regression guards on base (base never syncs).
